Phase 0.5 (deep map) was not run as a separate dispatch. The blast radius for this issue (activeIssueDir, gate-phase-entry.mjs, hooks.json, the ten replicated doc files) was established organically through six rounds of adversarial Phase 2 review, each citing and re-deriving the actual shared code -- arguably more thoroughly than a single map pass would have. Recorded as a deviation, not silently skipped.

Phase 2.5 (design bake-off) was skipped by explicit owner decision. After six rounds of adversarial spec iteration there was one viable design left (R4 as finally stated), not two genuinely different approaches to bake off; running the phase would have meant manufacturing a second sketch that did not need to exist.

Phase 4 round 1: BA's and DBA's REQUEST_CHANGES prose reads as 'the shipped gate is deterministically inert in production,' citing a suite run at passed=64/83 failed=3/83. The orchestrator independently reproduced this before accepting it: running the exact suite from plugins/pipeline/tests/ (the actual documented invocation, which run.sh's own line 9 cd's into regardless of caller cwd) gives clean 147/0 and 67/0; running the SAME file from the worktree root reproduces BA's exact numbers. DevOps independently diagnosed the same phenomenon as transient CPU contention from 5+ concurrent panelist run.sh processes on one host, not present on isolated CI runners, and got clean repeatable results once contention eased. QA independently ran both cwds, confirmed the split (147/0 vs 83/147), correctly characterized it as a non-hermetic test fixture (fixtures/*.mjs leaks process.cwd() into the synthetic payload) rather than a production defect, and separately, explicitly evaluated and REJECTED 'the gate abstains because #106 and #98 are both in-flight right now' as a finding at all -- it is the R4 design six rounds of Phase 2 review deliberately arrived at (abstain, unconditionally, on 2+ ambiguous candidates with no marker), already recorded in spec.json's open_questions[4]/R4(3)/AC42(i), with the marker's own missing producer already tracked as #111. DBA's realpath-vs-issue-dir-name dedup finding (a worktree and its main checkout both resolving to a directory named '106' inflating the candidate set) is judged a separate, real, NOT-previously-litigated gap and is carried into the delta round on that narrower ground, not on the 'gate is inert' framing. None of this discards BA's or DBA's verdicts -- both remain REQUEST_CHANGES and are owed a real response in the delta round -- but the round is NOT being treated as proof the shipped suite fails as documented, because directly re-running the documented command shows it does not.
